subject: Performance checklist & regional constraints — next steps
messages:
From: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@fincap.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Intro + perf targets for inference

Ben — thanks for yesterday's demo. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying items before we share this with our infra team:

• Primary use case: real-time scoring + streaming suggestions inside our trader UI (token-by-token streaming required).
• Target latency: p95 under 150ms for US/EU active markets, p99 budget up to 300ms during peaks.
• Peak concurrency: expect bursts to ~180 concurrent sessions (concurrent open sockets that request streaming tokens). Baseline concurrency ~40.
• Throughput profile: average response ~120 tokens, average sustained throughput target ~2,500 tokens/sec, peak short bursts up to 6,000 tokens/sec.
• Data residency: EU-only for user input and persisted logs; runtime telemetry (non-PII) may route to US for observability.

Anything we missed? Also attaching the template the infra team prefers for capacity planning.

— Sophie
Senior Platform Engineer, FinCap Technologies
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@fincap.co>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance checklist & regional constraints — next steps

Thanks Sophie — great summary and the template is helpful. Short answers / clarifications from our side and proposed next steps: 

1) Streaming: Redwood supports token-by-token streaming over HTTP/2 and WebSocket; we will validate connection behavior with your UI to confirm chunk sizing and flush frequency.
2) Latency SLOs: p95 <150ms in US/EU is achievable with a dedicated config (dedicated capacity + aggressive batching limits). P99 at 300ms during bursts is within our fallback tolerance if we enable fast-path kernels and prefix caching. We will produce a short performance profile showing p50/p95/p99 for candidate model families (7b/13b) under your token/sequence distribution.
3) Concurrency & throughput: your burst numbers are reasonable. To hit ~6k tok/s peaks we recommend a dedicated pool sized for concurrency + burst autoscale with a 3-minute warmup. We'll propose an initial sizing in the attached perf-template.
4) Data residency: we can enforce EU-only persistence for inputs and logs when you deploy under Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with regional pinning. Runtime routing for telemetry can be configured to forward anonymized metrics to our US Ops if you give explicit consent.

Next steps (proposed):
• Vivek and Monica to run a 1-hour perf validation using your sample traces (can you share a 10-minute representative trace with tokens and timestamps?).
• We’ll provide a model/quantization recommendation and a latency/throughput projection within 48 hours.
• Draft a short SOW addendum that locks region/residency language — Laura, can you own the SOW draft?

If that all sounds right I'll schedule the perf run for Wed morning US time.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sophie Nguyen <sophie@fincap.co>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance checklist & regional constraints — technical clarifications

Looping in quick technical clarifications so the perf run gives us actionable numbers: 

• Request shape: are most sessions single-stream (one request -> stream N tokens) or multi-turn (back-and-forth)? You mentioned suggestions inside UI — is that stateless or do you include short context history?
• Tokenization: what tokenizer / model family are you evaluating? We need tokenizer mapping to estimate RT token counts.
• Pinned region: is EU the only region for user-originated traffic, or will EU users sometimes route to US for lower latency? (affects routing policy).
• Failure tolerance: do you want automatic fallback to smaller model (13b -> 7b) in APAC / overflow? This affects quality/regression planning.

Action: Please drop a 10-minute trace (anonymized) into the Drive link or reply inline. I’ll prepare two test configs: (A) Dedicated EU pool optimized for p95<150ms, and (B) Cost-optimized mixed pool with fallback and APAC overflow routing. 

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Ramos <diego.r@fincap.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@fincap.co>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:41:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Performance checklist & regional constraints — validating trace upload

Ben/Vivek — we uploaded an anonymized 10-minute traffic trace to the Drive link (file: fincap_traces_20261123.jsonl). Quick notes: 

• Mostly single-stream suggestion requests with a 6–8 token prompt and ~120 token responses; ~30% of sessions include 1 turn of context.
• EU users originate to our EU gateways only; please assume EU persistence requirement for user data.
• We are okay with APAC overflow hitting a smaller model as long as probability of fallback <2% during core market hours.

Let us know the perf run slot — Wed 09:00 CET works best. We also uploaded a sample PII redaction spec for your compliance team to review.

Thanks,
Diego
Platform Ops, FinCap Technologies
